title: Boss: shape a help-desk ticket

job.text:
New domain, no training wheels. Your IT team pastes an outage note and asks the AI to "turn this into a ticket." The ticket system rejects anything missing a priority, and it needs affected systems as a real list, not one glued string. Shape the ask so a malformed ticket can't slip through.

Note: the live tool will add a free-text version of this ask in a later release — for now, pick the moves that pin the shape.

rows: Email and VPN both down since 9am

naivePrompt: Turn this outage note into a help-desk ticket.
basePrompt: Turn this outage note into a help-desk ticket.

text.plain: priority must be filled on every ticket. If the note doesn't say, set it to 'unspecified', never leave it out.
text.tech: priority is a required field; emit a placeholder when absent, never omit the key.

text.plain: When more than one system is affected, make affected_systems a list, one entry per system.
text.tech: affected_systems must be an array of strings, one element per system.

text.plain: Keep summary, priority, affected_systems on every ticket.
text.tech: Same keys on every ticket object.

text.plain: Add a severity emoji so it stands out.
text.tech: Add a severity emoji so it stands out.

text.plain: Make the ticket friendly and reassuring.
text.tech: Make the ticket friendly and reassuring.

rules.feedback: A ticket that can't slip through malformed. Priority is always present — 'unspecified' when the note is silent — and affected systems is a real list, so the system accepts it and you can see both outages at a glance.
rules.lesson: A shape with a required field and a list field rejects the malformed case.

output.source: a required priority + a list of systems

rules.feedback: The systems are a list now, but priority is gone. The note never stated a priority, so the AI quietly dropped the field — and the ticket system rejects a ticket with no priority. Make priority required too.
rules.lesson: A list field doesn't fix a missing required field.

rules.feedback: Priority is pinned, but two systems are glued into one string. "email and VPN" is a single value, so you can't filter or route by system. Make affected systems a real list.
rules.lesson: A required field doesn't fix two values crammed into one.

rules.claim: Done! Here's your ticket, with a friendly note. 🔴
rules.feedback: Malformed, and it looks fine. A severity emoji and a friendly tone changed the words, not the shape — priority is missing and both systems are jammed into one string, so the ticket system rejects it. Pin the shape instead.
rules.lesson: Tone and decoration don't make a ticket accepted.

cells: Email and VPN down 🔴 — hang in there!

hints.nudge: The ticket system rejects a ticket for two reasons. What are the two things every ticket must have?
hints.gap: This note never states a priority, and it names two systems. Which chips force a priority to always be present and let affected systems hold more than one?
hints.moves: Add Make priority required and Make affected systems a list. The emoji and friendly chips don't change what the system accepts.

whatYouDoDifferently.naive: "turn this into a ticket" → no priority, two systems glued, rejected.
whatYouDoDifferently.rewrite: "priority required, affected systems as a list" → a ticket the system accepts.

template.plain: Turn this into a ticket with these exact fields. Make [field] required — if it's not stated, write 'unspecified', never leave it out. When a field can have more than one value, make it a list.
template.tech: Emit a ticket object with these exact keys. [key] is required — use a placeholder if absent, never omit it. Multi-value fields must be arrays.

notes: ChatGPT: ask for the ticket as a small table or JSON; a missing field or a glued value means it ignored the shape.
Copilot in Excel: put each field in its own column and flag any empty required cell.
A chat AI that can't run code: read the ticket back field by field — a missing priority or two systems in one cell means re-ask. Never accept "it's all there" without checking each field.
